title: Conscious Processing and the Global Neuronal Workspace Hypothesis
authors: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux JP, Dehaene S.
why: How the global neuronal workspace explains conscious access.
caution: One theory of consciousness, not an uploading method.

title: Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain
authors: Dorkenwald S, Matsliah A, Sterling AR, Schlegel P, Yu SC, McKellar CE, Lin A, Costa M, Eichler K, Yin Y, Silversmith W, Schneider-Mizell C, Jordan CS, Brittain D, Halageri A, Kuehner K, Ogedengbe O, Morey R, Gager J, Kruk K, Perlman E, Yang R, Deutsch D, Bland D, Sorek M, Lu R, Macrina T, Lee K, Bae JA, Mu S, Nehoran B, Mitchell E, Popovych S, Wu J, Jia Z, Castro MA, Kemnitz N, Ih D, Bates AS, Eckstein N, Funke J, Collman F, Bock DD, Jefferis GSXE, Seung HS, Murthy M, FlyWire Consortium.
why: Maps the adult female fruit-fly brain at synapse scale.
caution: A wiring map is not a conscious emulation or a human brain upload.

title: A petavoxel fragment of human cerebral cortex reconstructed at nanoscale resolution
authors: Shapson-Coe A, Januszewski M, Berger DR, Pope A, Wu Y, Blakely T, Schalek RL, Li PH, Wang S, Maitin-Shepard J, Karlupia N, Dorkenwald S, Sjostedt E, Leavitt L, Lee D, Troidl J, Collman F, Bailey L, Fitzmaurice A, Kar R, Field B, Wu H, Wagner-Carena J, Aley D, Lau J, Lin Z, Wei D, Pfister H, Peleg A, Jain V, Lichtman JW.
why: Reconstructs a cubic millimeter of human cortex at nanoscale resolution.
caution: A small surgically removed tissue sample, not a whole human brain.

title: Functional connectomics spanning multiple areas of mouse visual cortex
why: Links mouse visual-cortex activity to dense electron-microscopy wiring.
caution: Mouse tissue and partial cortex; structure plus activity still leaves modeling gaps.

title: Reconstruction and Simulation of Neocortical Microcircuitry
authors: Markram H, Muller E, Ramaswamy S, Reimann MW, Abdellah M, Sanchez CA, Ailamaki A, Alonso-Nanclares L, Antille N, Arsever S, Kahou GA, Berger TK, Bilgili A, Buncic N, Chalimourda A, Chindemi G, Courcol JD, Delalondre F, Delattre V, Druckmann S, Dumusc R, Dynes J, Eilemann S, Gal E, Gevaert ME, Ghobril JP, Gidon A, Graham JW, Gupta A, Haenel V, Hay E, Heinis T, Hernando JB, Hines M, Kanari L, Keller D, Kenyon J, Khazen G, Kim Y, King JG, Kisvarday Z, Kumbhar P, Lasserre S, Le Bé JV, Magalhães BR, Merchán-Pérez A, Meystre J, Morrice BR, Muller J, Muñoz-Céspedes A, Muralidhar S, Muthurasa K, Nachbaur D, Newton TH, Nolte M, Ovcharenko A, Palacios J, Pastor L, Perin R, Ranjan R, Riachi I, Rodríguez JR, Riquelme JL, Rössert C, Sfyrakis K, Shi Y, Shillcock JC, Silberberg G, Silva R, Tauheed F, Telefont M, Toledo-Rodriguez M, Tränkler T, Van Geit W, Díaz JV, Walker R, Wang Y, Zaninetta SM, DeFelipe J, Hill SL, Segev I, Schürmann F.
why: Reconstructs and simulates a detailed juvenile-rat cortical microcircuit.
caution: A modeled microcircuit, not an entire rat or a transferred mind.

title: The Virtual Brain: a simulator of primate brain network dynamics
authors: Sanz Leon P, Knock SA, Woodman MM, Domide L, Mersmann J, McIntosh AR, Jirsa V.
why: Introduces personalized large-scale brain-network simulation software.
caution: Macroscopic brain dynamics do not establish subjective consciousness.

title: A large-scale model of the functioning brain
authors: Eliasmith C, Stewart TC, Choo X, Bekolay T, DeWolf T, Tang Y, Rasmussen D.
why: Spaun links a large spiking-neuron model to several behavioral tasks.
caution: Task performance in a simplified model does not prove consciousness.

title: Consciousness and complexity: a consilience of evidence
authors: Sarasso S, Casali AG, Casarotto S, Rosanova M, Sinigaglia C, Massimini M.
why: Reviews converging evidence for complexity-related measures of consciousness.
caution: Markers and theoretical interpretation, not a method for transferring consciousness.

title: Theories of consciousness
why: Compares major consciousness theories and how to test their differences.
caution: The theories disagree; no agreed test here proves an uploaded mind retains identity.

title: The human connectome: A structural description of the human brain
authors: Sporns O, Tononi G, Kötter R.
why: Sets out the human-connectome research program and its rationale.
caution: An influential structural roadmap, not a completed human synapse map.

title: Aldehyde-stabilized cryopreservation
why: Uses fixation and vitrification to preserve brain ultrastructure in rabbits and pigs.
caution: Chemical fixation preserves anatomy, not living function; no revival or memory recovery demonstrated.

title: State of Brain Emulation Report 2025
authors: Niccolò Zanichelli; Maximilian Schons; Isaak Freeman; Philip Shiu; Anton Arkhipov
why: Surveys neural dynamics, connectomics, emulation and embodiment as the building blocks of brain emulation.
caution: A progress report and research agenda, not evidence of human mind uploading.

title: The Fallacy of Favoring Gradual Replacement Mind Uploading Over Scan-and-Copy
authors: Keith B. Wiley; Randal A. Koene
why: Argues that gradual replacement and destructive scan-and-copy are equivalent with respect to personal identity.
caution: A contested philosophical argument, not an experiment. The arXiv record also lists a 2016 Journal of Consciousness Studies publication.

title: A theory of neural emulators
why: Proposes predictive neural emulators as an alternative route to functionally matching biological systems.
caution: Its claims about indistinguishable cognitive states are conjectures, not demonstrated consciousness transfer.

title: Neuromorphic Simulation of Drosophila Melanogaster Brain Connectome on Loihi 2
authors: Felix Wang; Bradley H. Theilman; Fred Rothganger; William Severa; Craig M. Vineyard; James B. Aimone
why: Maps an adult fruit-fly connectome model onto neuromorphic hardware and compares its dynamics with reference simulations.
caution: Simulation of a simplified fly network does not demonstrate consciousness, learned identity or a human upload.

title: Continuum of consciousness: Mind uploading and resurrection of human consciousness. Is there a place for physics, neuroscience and computers?
why: Uses a toy information-geometric model to explore a hypothetical migration of mental functions.
caution: Highly speculative thought experiment, not biological or clinical evidence for resurrection.

title: Ascribing Consciousness to Artificial Intelligence
why: Uses neuronal-replacement thought experiments to examine functionalism and integrated information theory.
caution: Conceptual analysis does not settle whether software is conscious or preserves a particular person.
